candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: coordinate interdisciplinary rehabilitation services, plan transitions of care, and individualize care according to client status and response.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — early individualized post-stroke rehabilitation planning
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate early rehabilitation assessment and planning—which should begin during hospitalization—from indiscriminate very-early high-dose mobilization; rehabilitation timing and intensity must be individualized to the client's condition.

options.A: Begin interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment and individualized planning during hospitalization, while tailoring mobilization intensity and timing to the client's medical and neurologic status rather than prescribing high-dose mobilization within the first 24 hours for everyone.
options.B: Postpone all rehabilitation assessment until after hospital discharge because early inpatient planning has no demonstrated relationship to functional recovery.
options.C: Require intensive out-of-bed mobilization within the first 24 hours for every stroke client because greater early mobilization doses consistently improve functional outcome.
options.D: Limit rehabilitation planning to clients with mild stroke because clients with moderate or severe deficits do not benefit from multidisciplinary assessment.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline supports comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment during hospitalization to determine the appropriate intensity and modality of rehabilitation. In-hospital interdisciplinary evaluation is associated with improved functional outcomes. However, the guideline also states that very early mobilization within 24 hours has not shown functional benefit, and one randomized trial found worse outcomes with high-dose very-early mobilization. B incorrectly delays planning. C converts early planning into an unsupported universal high-dose mobilization protocol. D incorrectly restricts rehabilitation assessment by stroke severity.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Early inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment and planning are supported after acute stroke, but this should not be conflated with universal intensive mobilization within the first 24 hours; mobilization timing and dose should be individualized.
candidate.source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
candidate.source_locator: Section 5.7 Rehabilitation — Synopsis: patients have diverse individualized needs and a comprehensive multidisciplinary program is critical for selecting rehabilitation intensity/modality; in-hospital interdisciplinary evaluation is associated with improved functional outcomes. The same synopsis states that very early (<24 hours) mobilization has not shown functional benefit and high doses produced worse outcomes in one RCT. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 1 supports multidisciplinary inpatient evaluation for the appropriate rehabilitation level.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
candidate.stem: A nurse participates in rehabilitation planning during the early hospitalization of a client with acute ischemic stroke. Which approach best reflects current guidance?
